audience.text: Java developers building or inspecting 3D scenes who need a free, open-source library with API compatibility to Aspose.3D for Java, using Maven Central for dependency management.

capabilities.text: Developers build 3D scene graphs using Scene, Node, and Entity, organizing geometry into parent-child hierarchies.
capabilities.title: Build 3D scene graphs

capabilities.text: Developers detect a 3D file's format automatically or resolve an explicit format from a file path or binary stream using FileFormat.detect and FileFormat.getFormatByExtension.
capabilities.title: Detect and resolve 3D file formats

capabilities.text: Developers generate primitive solids such as Box, Cylinder, Sphere, and Dish, each implementing toMesh() to produce a Mesh.
capabilities.title: Generate primitive geometry

capabilities.text: Developers define materials including PbrMaterial with albedo, metallic/roughness, occlusion, and emissive channels, and assign them per node via Node.setMaterial.
capabilities.title: Define and assign materials

capabilities.text: Developers model NURBS curves through NurbsCurve, exposing control points, knot vectors, degree, and order data.
capabilities.title: Model NURBS curves

capabilities.text: Developers work with Vector2/Vector3/Vector4, Matrix4, Quaternion, and BoundingBox for geometry and transform math.
capabilities.title: Perform math operations

capabilities.text: Developers import and export STL geometry (binary or ASCII) with StlLoadOptions/StlSaveOptions dispatched through Scene.fromFile and Scene.save.
capabilities.title: Import and export STL geometry

limitations.text: STL (import and export) is the only format that is fully functional in the published 26.5.0 package; other formats have recognized options classes but no working load/save path.
OBJ import has a real parser in the upstream source but ships as a stub in the currently published Maven Central artifact.
Several recognized-but-unfinished formats fail silently rather than throwing an error, so loading or saving can return successfully while producing no real data.
A handful of primitive-shape classes have a mesh-conversion method that is present but not yet implemented; Box, Cylinder, Sphere, and Dish are confirmed to convert correctly.
NurbsCurve exposes its full control-point/knot/degree data model, but sampling points along the curve is not yet implemented.
PbrSpecularMaterial's accessors are unimplemented in this edition; the PBR material capability uses the alternative that works.

problems_solved.text: Enables Java developers to build and inspect 3D scenes using a free, open-source library with API compatibility to the commercial Aspose.3D for Java product.
Provides automatic format detection and explicit format resolution for 3D files via FileFormat.detect and FileFormat.getFormatByExtension.
Supports importing and exporting STL geometry (binary or ASCII) end-to-end via Scene.fromFile and Scene.save with StlLoadOptions/StlSaveOptions.
Offers primitives such as Box, Cylinder, Sphere, and Dish that implement toMesh() to generate ready-to-use Mesh geometry.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Java is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed Java library implementing a clean-room API-compatible subset of Aspose.3D for Java, exposing the com.aspose.threed.* package for 3D scene graph manipulation.

uncertainties: The exact set of formats with stub implementations beyond STL and OBJ is not fully clarified by the facts; FILE_FORMATS.md is referenced but not included.
Whether the Scene rendering capability is entirely absent or merely unimplemented in this edition is not explicitly confirmed by the facts.
The scope of excluded functionality such as License, Metered, cryptographic helpers, and ZIP-packaged file-system read/write is described in the README but not independently verified by fact IDs.

workflows.name: Load and convert 3D files
workflows.text: Developers load a 3D file using Scene.fromFile with automatic format detection and save it to another format using Scene.save.

workflows.name: Build scene graphs
workflows.text: Developers construct a scene graph using Scene, Node, and Entity, attaching geometry via Node.addEntity or Node.createChildNode.

workflows.name: Assign materials
workflows.text: Developers define materials such as PbrMaterial with albedo, metallic, roughness, and emissive channels, then assign them to nodes via Node.setMaterial.

workflows.name: Inspect and manipulate transforms
workflows.text: Developers read and set node transforms using Matrix4, Quaternion, and Transform classes.

workflows.name: Define NURBS curves
workflows.text: Developers define NURBS curves by setting control points, knot vectors, degree, and order via NurbsCurve accessors.

workflows.name: Run tests
workflows.text: Developers run the test suite using JUnit 5, covering scene construction, vector math, format detection, STL round-tripping, glTF options, and NURBS curve data.
